Name: AlixLabs
Description:
Atomic Layer Etching for Nano Device Fabrication

We provide an ALE-based method of manufacturing nanostructures with characteristic size below 20nm.

This is a new method of nanostructure fabrication using the atomic layer etching process, which is inherently a damage-free etch process. Owing to the etching process’s selectivity to inclined surfaces, which has been recently discovered, the inclined surfaces can be used as a mask and in this way walls of tapered structures, which can be readily fabricated by e.g., dry etching or epitaxial growth, will provide masking during the atomic layer etching process. This is why this process provides access to fabrication of extremely small structures in a very precise and efficient way.

Name: Quantum Materials and nanoDevices Group at Chalmers University of Technology
Description:
Our group explores the frontiers of condensed matter physics by investigating quantum nanomaterials with a focus on two main research directions:

- Topological Insulators and Weyl Semimetals;
- High-Temperature Superconductors.

We adopt a comprehensive, interdisciplinary approach that spans the entire research pipeline — from material synthesis to device physics. Our work begins with the growth of high-quality thin films and nanostructures, including novel topological and superconducting compounds. We perform advanced structural and surface characterisation to understand and tune material properties at the atomic level.

Our team is also actively engaged in the nanofabrication of quantum devices in a cleanroom environment, developing custom architectures to probe quantum phenomena such as spin-momentum locking, proximity effects, quantum coherence, charge density waves, and more.

The final stage of our research focuses on electrical transport measurements, with experiments conducted down to the mK regime to uncover quantum phenomena that emerge only at ultra-low temperatures.

These experiments allow us to probe fundamental quantum effects and explore new phases of matter, with an eye toward future quantum technologies.

Name: PERSEUS EU Project
Description:
PERSEUS is an EU-funded research project pioneering a nanotechnology-based cancer treatment for deep-seated, drug-resistant, and metastatic tumours.

Nanotechnology in cancer care is still in its infancy, but PERSEUS aims to bridge this gap with specially engineered nano-systems made of multifunctional 2D layered nanocrystals. Activated by X-rays, these nanosystems are designed to provide multimodal therapy with minimal side effects. Instead of killing cancer cells directly, CT scanner X-rays trigger and image the nanosystems, which locally produce non-mutagenic oncolytic effects.

This process converts low-energy CT X-rays into reactive oxygen species, radiosensitising agents, and heat; it can also induce immunogenic cell death, exposing or releasing neo-antigens that trigger an anti-cancer immune response. Unlike visible or near-infrared light-based therapies, X-rays can penetrate and treat deep-seated tumours. In short, CT radiation acts as the spark that lights the match – a radical vision for an ambitious, high-risk project.

PERSEUS targets multiple cancers, including metastatic triple negative breast cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The nanosystems are biocompatible and inactive without CT radiation: they only activate where the CT beam is delivered, minimising side effects at distal sites.

The therapy is agnostic with respect to tumour type and gender incidence, since it is not affected by patient biochemistry – a second paradigm shift. PERSEUS unites physicists, chemists, engineers, biologists, physicians, pharmacologists, and radiologists to deliver a transformative nanotechnological approach to urgent, unmet clinical needs.

Description:
In short, our solution is about utilizing liquid flows in all heating and cooling systems and with a simple injection of HTF Compact during ongoing operation, increasing heat or cooling capacity which radically reduces electricity consumption and other loads on existing systems.

HTF Compact fits well in refrigeration and heating systems and reduces energy consumption by up to 40%

Nanofluids have been considered to be useful as advanced heat transfer fluids for almost two decades, as they have better suspension stability compared to micron solids, can flow smoothly without clogging the system and provide improved thermal and physical properties.




HTF Compact reduces the flow temperature in heat exchangers, whether they are water-to-water, water-to-air or refrigerant-to-water. Through a more efficient heat transfer, energy consumers (eg boiler, heat pump or cooling unit) run more efficiently and need to walk less to reach the desired temperature settings.




Our nanofluid has proven to be stable when circulated in closed systems and works well in black water found in our radiator systems or in various glycol mixtures in cooling systems and requires no extra effort to be installed and it can be installed without shutting down the system.




The nanoparticles in HTF Compact do not cause electrolysis, as they are oxides.

HTF Compact does not cause erosion or corrosion in pipe systems or equipment.

The main active component of HTF Compact is inert and non-carcinogenic.



HTF Compact concentration of 5% in the final system requires no change in installation, provides high flexibility to reach desired setpoints and is easy to install during operation. Through a simple water test and our questionnaire, you get a quick answer to what an installation of HTF Compact can provide for energy savings and what it costs.

With the help of our partners, we can also offer energy mapping, cleaning of existing systems, energy optimization of systems after installation of HTF .

Name: AMSwitch
Description:
AMSwitch is developing a new class of ultra‐low‐power logic switches using altermagnetic materials—an emerging magnetic state with zero net magnetization but electrically readable signals. These devices could operate below 1 aJ per bit, approaching fundamental energy limits.


The project explores two concepts: a gate‐tunable altermagnet switch using Berry‐curvature control, and a current‐driven switch that flips the altermagnetic order for compact logic operations. Together, they aim to enable reliable, non‐volatile, and energy‐efficient computing for future edge devices.


AMSwitch unites experts across materials science, nanoscale fabrication, device engineering, quantum theory, synchrotron characterization, and magnetometry—ensuring rapid progress from discovery to technology.


AMSwitch is coordinated by Chalmers University of Technology and has received funding from the European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA) under the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under Grant Agreement n° 101258102.
